concepts.name: Repository and working tree
concepts.summary: Recall that a repository stores a project's full history and that the working tree holds the current editable files.

concepts.name: Commits as snapshots
concepts.summary: Explain that a commit records a snapshot of the project with a message, author and link to its parent.

concepts.name: Staging area workflow
concepts.summary: Describe how changes move from the working tree to the staging area to a commit using add and commit.

concepts.name: Inspecting status and history
concepts.summary: Use status, log and diff to see what has changed and what has been recorded.

concepts.name: Local versus remote repositories
concepts.summary: Distinguish a local repository from a remote one and explain that cloning copies the full history.

concepts.name: Writing commit messages
concepts.summary: Understand why a commit message should briefly say what changed and why.

misconceptions.text: Git and GitHub are the same thing.
Git add saves the file to the repository as a commit.
A commit stores only the lines that changed rather than a snapshot of the project.

concepts.name: Branch creation and switching
concepts.summary: Create branches and switch between them to work on changes in isolation.

concepts.name: Push, fetch and pull
concepts.summary: Sync commits with a remote and tell fetch apart from pull.

concepts.name: Merging branches
concepts.summary: Merge one branch into another and recognise fast-forward versus merge-commit outcomes.

concepts.name: Resolving simple merge conflicts
concepts.summary: Read conflict markers, choose the correct content and complete the merge.

concepts.name: Ignoring files with gitignore
concepts.summary: Keep build output, dependencies and secrets out of version control using ignore patterns.

concepts.name: Undoing uncommitted changes
concepts.summary: Discard working-tree edits or unstage files without touching commits.

concepts.name: Amending the last commit
concepts.summary: Fix the most recent local commit's message or content before sharing it.

misconceptions.text: Git pull only downloads changes and never alters my working branch.
A merge conflict means something has broken and the repository is damaged.
Adding a file to gitignore removes it from the repository if it is already tracked.

concepts.name: Commit graph and references
concepts.summary: Analyse history as a graph of commits where branches, tags and HEAD are movable pointers.

concepts.name: Rebasing versus merging
concepts.summary: Compare how rebase and merge integrate work and the history each produces.

concepts.name: Interactive rebase cleanup
concepts.summary: Reorder, squash and reword local commits to produce a clean, reviewable history.

concepts.name: Reset, revert and restore
concepts.summary: Choose among reset modes and revert based on whether history is shared and what must be preserved.

concepts.name: Recovery with reflog
concepts.summary: Find and restore lost commits after a bad reset, rebase or deleted branch.

concepts.name: Stashing and cherry-picking
concepts.summary: Shelve unfinished work and apply individual commits to another branch.

concepts.name: Tracking branches and upstreams
concepts.summary: Explain how remote-tracking branches relate to local ones and diagnose ahead/behind/diverged states.

concepts.name: Pull request workflow
concepts.summary: Use short-lived feature branches, pull requests and review to integrate changes into a shared branch.

misconceptions.text: Branches are separate copies of the code rather than pointers to commits.
Git reset --hard is always safe because Git keeps everything.
Rebase is always better than merge because it gives a cleaner history.

concepts.name: Branching strategy selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate trunk-based, Gitflow and similar strategies against team size, release cadence and risk.

concepts.name: Rewriting shared history safely
concepts.summary: Judge when rewriting published history is acceptable and use force-with-lease and team coordination to limit damage.

concepts.name: Bisecting regressions
concepts.summary: Locate the commit that introduced a bug using binary search, ideally automated with a test script.

concepts.name: Complex conflict resolution
concepts.summary: Analyse conflicts using the merge base and both sides, and reuse resolutions across repeated rebases.

concepts.name: Worktrees and submodules
concepts.summary: Choose among worktrees, submodules and subtrees for parallel checkouts and nested dependencies.

concepts.name: Hooks and automated checks
concepts.summary: Assess where local hooks, server-side rules and CI should enforce quality and message conventions.

concepts.name: Signed commits and provenance
concepts.summary: Explain how commit signing verifies authorship and judge when to require it.

concepts.name: Removing sensitive data from history
concepts.summary: Evaluate remediation of committed secrets, including rotation and history rewriting.

misconceptions.text: Deleting a leaked secret in a new commit removes the exposure.
One branching model such as Gitflow suits every team.
Client-side hooks guarantee that rules are enforced for everyone.

concepts.name: Git object model internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate behaviour and performance through the model of content-addressed blobs, trees, commits and tags.

concepts.name: Packfiles and repository maintenance
concepts.summary: Diagnose repository size and speed issues using packing, garbage collection and maintenance tasks.

concepts.name: Scaling large repositories
concepts.summary: Design workflows for very large repositories using partial clones, sparse checkout and shallow history.

concepts.name: Custom merge strategies and drivers
concepts.summary: Create attribute-based merge, diff and filter rules for special file types.

concepts.name: Repository migration and history surgery
concepts.summary: Plan migrations, splits and merges of repositories while preserving meaningful history and references.

concepts.name: Team Git policy design
concepts.summary: Design branch protection, review, signing and release tagging policies that fit an organisation's risk profile.

concepts.name: Plumbing commands and scripting
concepts.summary: Use low-level commands to script reliable tooling and inspect or repair repository state.

misconceptions.text: Git stores history as a chain of diffs between versions.
Shallow or partial clones are just smaller full clones with no workflow trade-offs.
Rewriting history with filter tools leaves old commits unreachable everywhere immediately.
